new_user_requirements.title: The complete current onboarding semantics constitute hIRC's architecture rather than an optional add-on
new_user_requirements.acceptance: Every operational path binds the exact active foundation and its whole-source coverage; safe inspection/repair is the only fallback when the binding is invalid

new_user_requirements.title: Ordinary hIRC behavior embodies the foundation without requiring users to know or repeatedly see its internal terminology
new_user_requirements.acceptance: Representative workflows preserve the same evidence, authority, privacy, refusal, correction, autonomy, and recovery behavior in plain domain language; authorized inspectors retain exact traceability

new_user_requirements.title: The foundational architecture evolves fluidly in real time as the system improves
new_user_requirements.acceptance: Source-bound candidate versions compile, test, migrate, activate transactionally, remain visible per active work, and roll back or recover without silent semantic drift or self-authorized evaluator changes

changes.change: Bind the current selected English Epistemethics 3.0, VowOS2026, Grand Plan, and effective review-integrity source; retain 1.0 bindings as historical provenance.
Make the complete formation and governing semantics an always-active, versioned foundation kernel rather than an optional prompt/onboarding subsystem.
Express foundation behavior in plain domain language by default while preserving authorized traceability to exact source and compiled rules.
Classify prototype tests as source-reported and not independently rerunnable from this transfer until the exact fingerprinted source objects are admitted and rerun.
Remove the advanced temporary-subagent unban and mark U064 superseded; test every indirect actor-creation path.
Add a normative system-wide threat model, trust domains, security invariants, attacker capabilities, assumptions, controls, residuals, evidence, and owners before implementation.

Define phishing-resistant human identity, unique workload/system identity, purpose-separated roots, metadata-only secret catalog, short-lived credentials, rotation/revocation, and strongest-path recovery.

Select and threat-model the desktop shell; sandbox the renderer, narrow IPC, protect loopback APIs, enforce CSP/injection controls, and add a fixed trusted identity/target/authority strip and Safe hIRC.

Treat the frontier registry as a dated candidate seed; require exact-route discovery, compatibility and privacy probes, minimal egress manifests, local tool authorization, recorded actual configuration, and isolated fallbacks.

Separate organization planning, permanent identity reservation, formation/admission, minimum capability, budget reservation, and runtime activation; a bulk approval cannot bypass per-actor invariants.

Treat the attention governor as a security control plane with non-suppressible classes, separate classification/presentation, independent health, auditable overrides, anti-coercion tests, and Safe hIRC bypass.

Run extensions out of process with no ambient authority; add digest/dependency pinning, explicit capabilities, quotas, SSRF/DNS-rebinding controls, safe disable/removal, vulnerability state, and rollback.

Bind consequential mutations to immutable revision, audit, and outbox atomically; enumerate and negative-test admin/import/migration/retry/restore/direct-database bypasses and anchor checkpoints outside the database.

Separate build, online control, release, and recovery authorities; require locked inputs, isolated builds, SBOM, authenticated provenance, immutable artifacts, a pinned TUF profile, signed security floors, and verified rollback/forward recovery.
Split the Bridge into a network gateway, deterministic contract broker, isolated minimized bridgekeeper, and local release/ingress gate with separate identities and interfaces.

Specify peer enrollment, out-of-band verification, canonical signed envelopes, current TLS application profile, purpose-separated keys, sequence/nonces, expiry, downgrade rejection, offline revocation limits, key rotation/recovery, and compromise containment; prohibit custom production crypto.

Divide federation into specification, offline conformance, two-system lab, hostile lab, independent assessment, bounded pilot, and separately authorized broader activation; keep it disabled until every applicable gate passes.

Define field-level data ownership, purpose, processors, egress, retention, disposition, residency, and derived-data inheritance; preserve the conservative no-free-text federation profile pending an owner decision.
Make source-bound milestone reflection and lens refinement an architecture-native event that updates the next milestone's threats, requirements, tests, and plan without becoming a recitation ritual.

Expand the adversarial matrix for identity cloning, key theft/rotation, contract forks, canonicalization/parser differential, replay and 0-RTT, malicious updates, UI/IPC attacks, SSRF/rebinding, database-owner attack, backup/key loss, privacy side channels, attention coercion, and clean-room recovery.

Move foundation binding, threat model, identity, secrets, signed commands/results, atomic audit/outbox, recovery, and kill switch into P0/P1 before a provider can create effects; retain P6 as noncritical.

Add ADRs for foundation versioning, desktop shell, authorization model, identity/PKI, secret topology, bridge protocol, cryptographic profile, provider privacy, audit anchoring, build/release trust, and recovery custody.
Add predecessor/supersession, rationale, security/privacy impact, governing source, dependencies, acceptance tests, and evidence status so corrections do not overwrite original user meaning.

Retain bounded owner decisions for richer cross-system free text, the first-release human-principal model, the first assurance/compliance profile, and genuinely independent release/recovery/bridge custodians; continue safe local-core work without guessing them or simulating quorum.
